newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals drift within range.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals drift within range.

text.p: Precious metals prices drifted within range as volumes remained light on Thursday afternoon.
Dealers said there was insufficient momentum behind the market to take gold far away in either direction from its high of $369.60 per ounce bid which was also the morning fix.
The afternoon fixing came in at $369.00. On Wednesday afternoon the fixing was $368.70.
At the fixing Comex January was up $0.80 at $370.50.
"Activity is slowing down and business has been very quiet. We have not seen any real new trend in gold so far," according to an analyst based in continental Europe.
Dealers said there was no trend in the price overnight.

To establish a direction gold would have to get into the $372-$373 range and that would mean taking out resistance at $370 on the way abd trhat was unlikely ahead of the Christmas holiday next week and New Year the week after.
However, dealers in London pointed out that the market's lack of liquidity could mean a relatively volatile session, albeit in a fairly tight range.
"No new business is expected before Christmas. The producers and funds have done what they had to do and industrial interest will not be back before January," one market professional said.
The OTC option expiry on Friday was likely to feature the $370 strike price, given that the market had been hovering below that level since December 9.
"I'd be surprised if the option expiry had much of an impact at this stage in the year," a dealer said.
Silver picked up on fund buying in New York on Wednesday afternoon and following a static morning in London, added only a couple of cent to its unchanged opening of $4.85/$4.87.
A move into the $4.90s would mean the price attracting selling from the pile of physical silver hanging over the market.
"Heavy selling could be expected approaching $5.00 but support was available at $4.70," an analyst said.
Platinum was indicated at $371.00/$372.00, up 50 cents overnight but unchanged from the opening.
"Almost all of platinum's gains have been from short-covering. There hasn't been any new buying," he said.
Palladium was very quiet and 25 cents higher at $118.00/$119.00.
